== Biography ==
The retained child account places Peter's birth before 31 October 1790, uncertain, and names [[Glasgow-1382|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Davidson-14073|Christine Davidson]] as parents. The existing 97% father assessment concerns that recorded child and family; maternity is not separately graded. An earlier draft also estimated a birth about 1810 for Peter. That later estimate and the Agnes Scott adult household remain a separate identity proposition from the 1790 child. The memorial Peter, whose derivative death readings are 1810 aged19 or 1819 aged48, is a third unresolved comparison. No join among these propositions is established by the shared name.

=== Livingston monument Peter comparison, 24 October 2026 ===

The Livingston family monument names a Peter Glasgow as Thomas and Christian's son or Janet's brother, but its two Findmypast derivatives read 12 September 1810 aged 19 and 12 September 1819 aged 48. The public BillionGraves index lists Peter in this family without resolving the original inscription. Neither death is assignable to [[Glasgow-1450]]: his current adult account has Agnes Scott and children in the 1840s, while the two monumental readings also contradict one another.<ref name="LivingstonMI2026">Findmypast, Scotland Monumental Inscriptions, Livingston, derivative transcriptions [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00422894&tab=this PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00422894] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511321&tab=this GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511321] (captured 24 October 2026); compare [https://billiongraves.com/grave/Thomas-Glasgow/3399144 BillionGraves, Thomas Glasgow, marker LV 106], public index checked 24 October 2026. The BillionGraves photo preview is blurred and the original inscription was not independently read. The three derivative accounts conflict on years, ages and some dates; they are not three independent witnesses to a precise vital fact.</ref>

Keep the 1790 record-defined child, this profile's later adult household, and the memorial Peter as distinct identity propositions pending the original stone and independent later-life evidence. Preserve the existing 97% father assessment with its recorded-child/adult-identity scope for now; this source alone neither proves a merger nor warrants a new Peter profile or automatic regrade.
